name: Summand
tagline: Validate XRechnung, ZUGFeRD and Factur-X e-invoices against EN 16931 in pure TypeScript: in Node, the browser and at the edge, without Java.
seoTitle: Summand – XRechnung, ZUGFeRD and Factur-X validator for TypeScript (EN 16931, no Java)
description:
Germany requires businesses to receive e-invoices since 1 January 2025, and to send them from 2027. Checking an XRechnung or ZUGFeRD invoice has so far meant the KoSIT validator: Java, Saxon and a server. Summand runs the same official rule sets in pure TypeScript, so you can check invoices in your Node backend, in a serverless function, in the browser before upload, or in CI.

Summand ships its own XPath 2.0 and Schematron engine and the official EN 16931 rules from CEN (UBL and CII) and the XRechnung rules from KoSIT, including the severity changes KoSIT applies for the standard, extension and CVD profiles. It passes all 1'142 CEN rule tests and every invoice of the KoSIT test suite. It reads the XML embedded in ZUGFeRD and Factur-X PDFs, recognises the profile, checks Leitweg-IDs and reports every finding with rule, message, XPath and line. Summand checks invoices technically; it is not tax advice.

faq.q: Does Summand replace the KoSIT validator?
faq.a: For the business rules, yes: Summand runs the same official Schematron files and passes the KoSIT test suite. It does not check the XML schemas (XSD) yet, so a document with an element in the wrong place can pass Summand and still fail the KoSIT validator. Schema validation is on the roadmap.

XRechnung 3.0 in UBL and CII, ZUGFeRD 2.x and Factur-X as PDF or XML, Peppol BIS and plain EN 16931 invoices. ZUGFeRD 1.0 predates EN 16931 and is reported as unsupported. Factur-X MINIMUM and BASIC WL are recognised but are not full invoices under EN 16931, which Summand says in the result.

faq.q: Does an invoice that passes meet the German VAT rules?
faq.a: Not automatically. Summand checks the technical rules of EN 16931 and XRechnung. Whether an invoice is correct for VAT purposes, for example the tax rate or an exemption, is a question for your accounting or tax adviser.
No. It runs where you call it: on your server, in your function or in the browser. Nothing is uploaded, and the Pro packages do not contact a licence server either.

faq.q: Why are the rule sets under other licences?
faq.a: Summand's code is MIT. The bundled rules are the official artefacts: EN 16931 from CEN under the EUPL 1.2 and XRechnung from KoSIT under the Apache License 2.0. Both allow this use; the notices ship with the package.
